explanation: The game was fashionable at Badminton House, the Duke of Beaufort's estate in Gloucestershire, in the 1870s. It grew from the old children's game battledore and shuttlecock.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The sources agree that the game took its name from the Duke of Beaufort's Badminton House in Gloucestershire, but they disagree on when it was first played there. Most give 1873, while others point to earlier dates. 1873 is the most common date. Britannica says the game was first played at the estate of the 9th Duke of Beaufort, Henry Somerset, about 1873. Earlier dates. Badminton England says the Duke held parties at the house in 1863. Olympics.com's Paris 2024 page says it was sometime in the early 1860s. The Badminton World Federation's guide dates the game's development at the house to between 1856 and 1859. Origins are uncertain. Wikipedia says the name's derivation from the house is clear, but why or when remains unclear. It also notes that as early as 1860, a London toy dealer named Isaac Spratt published a booklet titled Badminton Battledore – A New Game, though no copy survives. The 1873 date is the one most widely repeated, but the sources conflict and the earliest play at the estate is not firmly documented.
